features: THE ACCOUNT THAT HAD NEVER BEEN CLOSED — Every building's chart of accounts holds account 2202, «Amounts owed to the Revenue for withholding tax», which until now only knew how to fill up: every payment to a supplier subject to withholding made it grow, but the movement that settles that debt did not exist in the software. Verified before a line of code was written: across every building in the database that account had credits and not one single debit. From this version the withholding tax F24 is prepared, paid and closed inside the software.

THIS VERSION CHANGES THE DATABASE: three new tables for the F24 payment forms, their lines and the link to the payments they cover. No existing table is touched — these are creations only — which is the safest possible shape for the upgrade from 1.9.x, the one upgrade without an automatic backup.

New «Withholding tax and F24» entry in the Movements menu: the deadline list answers the question you ask yourself on the 16th of the month — do I owe anything, and how much? Until now the answer had to be rebuilt by hand, payment by payment, applying two different thresholds and three deadline rules that are easy to confuse.

THE TWO THRESHOLDS, WHICH ARE NOT THE SAME THING. A building does not pay on every payment: it accumulates. For works and services contracts (4%) you pay once the running total reaches €500, and in any case by 16 June and 16 December. For professionals (20%) the threshold is €100 and there is only ONE annual cut-off, 16 December. The two accumulators are separate: €300 of contracts plus €300 of professional fees do not make €600 of threshold reached — they are two distinct obligations. Withholdings made in December are paid by 16 January of the following year, under both regimes.

Deadlines really do shift: if the 16th falls on a Saturday or a public holiday the term moves to the next working day, national holidays included — Easter Monday among them, which being movable can land exactly there.

THE TRANSCRIPTION SHEET. The payment form's detail shows the fields in the order of the F24 model — tax code, instalment, reference month and year, amount — ready to copy to the clipboard or print on a clean sheet, to keep on file or hand to the accountant. It is not the ministerial form, which is for paying over the counter and will come: it is what you need to fill in the F24 in your online banking or on the Revenue's website, which is how it actually gets paid. Below the sheet, each line lists the payments it is settling, with supplier and date: the answer to the question that arrives six months later, «what were these €320 for?».

Recording the payment closes the account, with two double-entry lines: DEBIT 2202, CREDIT bank. From that moment the form is no longer amended, it is reversed: a payment to the Revenue is something that happened, and it is corrected by writing the equal and opposite movement, not by rewriting the past. After a reversal the withholdings become payable again and re-enter the next calculation. The «Update deadlines» button turns amber with a count when there are withholdings not yet in any form: when it is white, the list is already up to date.

Fixed — EDITING A PAYMENT WITHOUT RESENDING THE WITHHOLDING ZEROED IT. An absent field was read as «zero» rather than «leave alone», and invoice allocations cannot even be changed on that screen: there was no legitimate way to declare that the withholding was gone. Now absent means absent, and an amount that does not match the invoices being paid is rejected rather than accepted — it used to be a snapshot, with this version it becomes the figure paid to the Revenue.

Fixed — REVERSING A PAYMENT LEFT ITS REMINDER OPEN, still asking for a withholding the reversal had already cancelled: it could only be closed by hand, by whoever noticed it was no longer needed. It now closes by itself.

Fixed — THE DEADLINE CALCULATION IGNORED PUBLIC HOLIDAYS. It handled Saturday and Sunday and nothing else, so a deadline on a holiday was offered as valid. The real case is Easter Monday, which being movable can fall on the 16th or on the Monday you shift to from a Sunday — and the old calculation, in that second case, did not shift a second time.

Fixed — THE BALANCE SHEET WIDGET WAS HARD TO READ WHEN IT REPORTED A PROBLEM. Its text used greys chosen for a white background: on the error red the contrast collapsed and the Assets/Liabilities equation became a shadow, precisely when those numbers matter most.

Worth knowing: draft forms have no accounting effect and do not appear in the Journal, because the entry is only created when you record the payment — the form's detail now says so, since a missing movement is easy to mistake for missing data. The building's tax code is mandatory on the F24: if it is absent the detail flags it and says where to enter it, rather than letting you discover it in front of a half-filled form.

Under the hood: the calculation of when to pay is a pure function with no stored counters, so it is recomputed from scratch every time and regenerating drafts can never do harm. The thresholds live in one place only and the screen does not restate them — it receives them, so the day they change one file is touched and the guide stops repeating a superseded number by itself. The snapshot of the supplier's tax data saved with every payment now includes the withholding regime, because correcting a supplier record today must not reclassify payments already made. Thirty-four new tests cover the three deadline rules, the holiday calendar, form generation, the closing of account 2202 and its reversal.
